methodological_rigor.justification: Multi-institutional (three US academic centers) retrospective real-world analysis of 117 patients on a commercially available tumor-informed ctDNA assay (Signatera). The approach (logistic regression for response, Cox for survival with KM curves and log-rank) is appropriate for the question. Weaknesses include retrospective design, heterogeneous regimens (dual ICI, PD-1+LAG-3, monotherapy) in a modest sample, immortal time bias potential (landmark at 3-4 weeks requires patients to survive to the second measurement), inconsistent handling of the undetectable-at-baseline subgroup (placed in 'decrease' group), and no multivariable adjustment for stage, regimen, or LDH. The eventual-clearance analysis mixes response to therapy and post-landmark interventions (RT, resection) acknowledged in only 6 of 9 cases. No correction for multiple testing.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Early ctDNA dynamics at 3-4 weeks as a predictor of ICI response and survival in advanced melanoma is a clinically useful concept that could support response-adapted treatment. The observed effect sizes (OR ~30 for DCR, HR 0.18 for PFS, HR 0.28 for OS) are large and clinically relevant. The study uses a commercially available, deployable assay. This is a retrospective multi-institutional cohort, Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical impact depends on prospective validation explicitly called for by the authors.

reporting_quality.justification: This is a biomarker prognostic/predictive study, best mapped to REMARK (or STROBE for observational design). Basic items are covered: patient population, inclusion criteria, assay details (Signatera), endpoint definitions, statistical methods, and confidence intervals. Several REMARK items are under-reported: no biomarker threshold pre-specification, no adjustment for standard prognostic factors (LDH, stage, regimen) in multivariable models, no handling of censoring in a pre-specified landmark analysis, and no sample-size justification. No data availability statement visible in extracted text; Signatera is commercial so raw data release is inherently limited.

novelty_literature.justification: ctDNA dynamics as a predictor of ICI response in melanoma is not new: Bratman et al. (2020, ref 23) and Eroglu et al. (2023, ref 22) have already established similar concepts in melanoma and solid tumors. The incremental novelty here is the very early 3-4 week landmark (vs 6-9 weeks previously), use of a commercial tumor-informed assay, and a multi-institutional real-world setting with 117 patients. This is a meaningful but incremental extension rather than a fundamental discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and well structured with a logical flow from background to methods to results to discussion. Tables and figures (treatment response bars, Kaplan-Meier curves, spider plots of ctDNA kinetics) appear appropriate. The discussion is measured, acknowledges limitations, and appropriately contrasts ctDNA with FDG-PET/CT and other biomarkers. One references note 'Reference deleted' which is unusual. Minor grammatical issues and some reporting gaps.

key_strengths: Multi-institutional real-world cohort of 117 advanced melanoma patients with paired baseline and 3-4 week ctDNA measurements
Very large effect sizes (OR 30.56 for DCR; HR 0.18 PFS, 0.28 OS) suggesting strong biomarker signal even if partly driven by selection
Early landmark (3-4 weeks) earlier than prior ICI ctDNA studies, relevant for treatment adjustment
Pseudoprogression subgroup (5 patients) and ctDNA-clearance analysis provide useful clinical context
key_concerns: Retrospective design with no multivariable adjustment for stage, regimen type, baseline LDH, or prior therapy
Heterogeneous ICI regimens (ipi/nivo 57%, nivo/relatlimab 20%, anti-PD-1 mono 23%) collapsed in primary analysis
Undetectable-at-baseline patients (13.7%) classified in the decrease group may bias effect estimates upward
Landmark at 3-4 weeks introduces potential immortal-time bias; no formal landmark analysis framework described
Eventual ctDNA clearance subgroup (9 of 41 with initial increase) mixed with post-landmark interventions (RT, resection) in 6/9 cases
Incremental rather than novel biomarker concept; prospective validation is explicitly required
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent retrospective multi-institutional real-world ctDNA study with clinically relevant findings but meaningful methodological limitations and incremental novelty; tier 3 (e.g., JCO Precision Oncology scope at upper end, otherwise European Journal of Cancer / Cancers) is defensible with minor revisions. Tier 2 would require more rigorous multivariable modeling and landmark analysis.
